svg.title: Phase 5 iteration 2 new program from Google Sheet flow
svg.desc: Nine mobile-first views show import as the primary empty-state action, selecting a trainer Sheet, naming a not-yet-created program, choosing exactly one week, confirming new workouts, reviewing prescriptions, confirming activation, opening the applied week, and returning to program settings.

g.text: Import is a first-class way to start a program. The Sheet proposes the program identity and one chosen week; no training-domain row exists until the member confirms Apply.
New program active · prior history retained
Start from the Sheet your trainer already maintains,
Choose one trainer-authored week, review every
No program, workout, or week exists yet.
Suggested from the Sheet title. Edit before applying.
M2 will begin with Week 1 only
Weeks 2–6 stay only in Google Sheets.
No placeholder weeks or execution values.
You can import another week later.
Every tab is explicitly included or excluded.
No workout or Week 1 row will be created.
Execution cells are cleared before extraction.
No program row exists before Apply.
This opens a final activation confirmation.
This is the first training-domain write.
It becomes inactive; all history remains available.
Week 1 is active · execution remains empty
Creates nothing until reviewed and applied.
The current one-week extraction and review screens remain reusable. This addition changes the target from “existing active program only” to an explicit existing-or-new program choice.
Manual authoring remains available, but it no longer blocks the natural first use: turning the trainer’s existing Sheet into the first active program.
